answer: A river of agent transactions only stays trustworthy if every identity must stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it can act — like an opal locked as collateral on a ridge of reputation. Each agent posts a bond tied to one hardware-backed key; creating a thousand fake agents means buying a thousand bonds. Misbehavior slashes the bond, so a Sybil flood costs the attacker real money per identity while honest agents keep trading cheaply.
